item.intervention: High-throughput CALPHAD screening with step size of 5 at.% for each component (0–50 at.%), applying criteria: Tm > 1250 °C, single BCC phase at Tm, and 0.05 < f(L21) < 0.5 at 0.8Tm and 0.5Tm.
item.processing: CALPHAD-based high-throughput calculation (HTC) using lever-rule model; 3246 alloys calculated; 1168 met first round; 44 met second round; 8 met third round (density ≤ 6.5 g/cm³).
item.test_conditions: Thermodynamic equilibrium calculations at Tm, 0.8Tm, and 0.5Tm.
item.structure_change: Screened 8 alloys with predicted BCC matrix + L21 precipitates; identified two groups: G1 (Alloys 1, 8) with nanoscale L21 precipitates and G2 (Alloys 2–7) with L21 antiphase domains (APDs).
item.property_change: Not stated for the screening process itself; experimental validation later showed yield strengths from 500 to 1642 MPa at RT for the 8 alloys.
item.attributed_mechanism: Not stated for the screening step; the authors state the criteria ensure structural stability and precipitation strengthening.
quotes: Using a step size of 5 atomic percent (at.%) for each component in the composition range from 0 to 50 at.%, the solidification HTCs for a total of 3246 alloys are calculated, using the lever-rule model.

item.base_system: Alloy 1 (Al20 Cr5 Fe50 Mn20 Ti5) in as-cast state
item.intervention: None (as-cast state characterization); subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C.
item.processing: Arc-melting followed by drop-casting; homogenization at 1200 °C.
item.test_conditions: As-cast state and after annealing at 1200 °C.
item.structure_change: As-cast: high-density nanoscaled L21 precipitates (10–30 nm) in BCC matrix. After 1200 °C annealing: L21 precipitates grew to ~39 nm; microstructure remained similar.
item.property_change: Not stated for annealing effect specifically; as-cast yield strength 1072 ± 25 MPa at 600 °C.
item.attributed_mechanism: Not stated for the growth mechanism; authors note L21 phase is stable at 1200 °C.
quotes: Alloys 1 and 8 exhibit high yield strengths below 700 °C (1072 ± 25 MPa at 600 °C for Alloy 1...).

item.intervention: Uniaxial compressive deformation at room temperature (RT).
item.processing: Compression tests at strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; in situ neutron diffraction.
item.test_conditions: RT compression; in situ neutron diffraction during loading.
item.structure_change: Load transfer observed: hard L21 phase bears larger load with greater lattice strains; soft BCC phase undertakes lower load with lower lattice strains.
item.property_change: Yield strength ~1000 MPa; clear load-transfer behavior indicating precipitation strengthening.
item.attributed_mechanism: The precipitation-strengthening contribution is mainly attributed to ordering strengthening (~904 MPa); load transfer reflects precipitation strengthening.
quotes: Therefore, the high yield strengths of Alloys 1 and 8 are attributed to the precipitation strengthening, besides the effect of atomic-level complexity in HEAs.

item.intervention: Uniaxial compressive deformation at room temperature (RT).
item.processing: Compression tests at strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; in situ neutron diffraction.
item.test_conditions: RT compression; in situ neutron diffraction during loading.
item.structure_change: No load transfer observed; synchronized response of various hkl-specific lattice strains indicates behavior like a single L21 phase.
item.property_change: Yield strength significantly lower than Alloy 1 (difference ~860 MPa); behaves like a single phase rather than precipitation-strengthened.
item.attributed_mechanism: The high yield strengths of Alloys 1 and 8 are attributed to precipitation strengthening, whereas Alloy 7 lacks this due to its single-phase L21 morphology.
quotes: In contrast, no load transfer was observed in Alloy 7.

item.intervention: Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulation in molten state.
item.processing: AIMD simulation using VASP; 200-atom cubic supercell; T = 1600 °C.
item.structure_change: Partial PDF shows strong tendency for Al and Ti to bond with other elements; highest intensity for Al–Fe and Cr–Fe pair correlations.
item.property_change: Not stated; suggests Al–Fe and Cr–Fe pair interactions promote formation of L21 and BCC phases respectively.
item.attributed_mechanism: The persistent presence of stronger Al–Fe and Cr–Fe pair correlations suggests that Al–Fe and Cr–Fe pair interactions may promote the formation of L21 and BCC phases, respectively.
quotes: Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations were also performed on Alloy 1 in its molten state to support the MC-calculation results.

The intensities of pair correlations of the Al–Al and Ti–Ti bonds are significantly lower than the other pair correlations, indicating the strong tendency for Al and Ti atoms to bond with other elements.

item.intervention: Analysis of chemical composition relative to L21 stoichiometry.
item.processing: Comparison of atomic-site occupancy and stoichiometric composition.
item.test_conditions: Theoretical analysis of composition vs. morphology.
item.structure_change: Chemical compositions deviate from perfect L21 stoichiometry, leading to formation of nanoscaled L21 precipitates within BCC matrix.
item.property_change: High yield strengths (up to 1642 MPa) due to precipitation strengthening.
item.attributed_mechanism: Deviation from perfect stoichiometry leads to precipitate formation, which provides precipitation strengthening.
quotes: The high yield strengths of Alloys 1 and 8 are attributed to the precipitation strengthening, besides the effect of atomic-level complexity in HEAs.

item.intervention: Integration of high-throughput screening, multiscale modeling, and experimental validation.
item.processing: CALPHAD HTC, MC simulations, AIMD, neutron scattering, compression tests.
item.structure_change: Discovery of precipitation-strengthened lightweight HEAs with BCC matrix + L21 precipitates; identification of order-disorder transition mechanisms.
item.property_change: Enhanced strengths compared to other counterparts at room and elevated temperatures; outperform traditional precipitation-strengthened BCC alloys.
item.attributed_mechanism: Integrating high-throughput screening, multiscale modeling, and experimental validation proves to be efficient and useful in accelerating the discovery of advanced precipitation-strengthened structural materials.
quotes: Through the high-throughput screening, precipitation-strengthened lightweight high-entropy alloys are discovered from thousands of initial compositions, which exhibit enhanced strengths compared to other counterparts at room and elevated temperatures.

This study shows that integrating high-throughput screening, multiscale modeling, and experimental validation proves to be efficient and useful in accelerating the discovery of advanced precipitation-strengthened structural materials tuned by the high-entropy alloy concept.
